lines.caption: This is a tour of pull request 62, which makes CI's code review skip work another review covers, and run lighter.
lines.say: This is a tour of pull request sixty-two, which makes CI's code review skip work another review covers, and run lighter.

lines.caption: It has three parts: what the PR adds, how it was built and verified, and what comes later.
Part 1. What this PR adds.
Two new reasons to skip a review, and a lighter review with a time limit.
First, the plan step asks GitHub whether a newer push has started its own run. If so, the review is skipped at once.
Otherwise it waits up to 20 minutes for earlier runs, then checks again for a newer run.
lines.say: Otherwise it waits up to twenty minutes for earlier runs, then checks again for a newer run.

lines.caption: A head that the review state records as CI's own fix, on top of the reviewed head, is skipped too.
The older rules still apply: an already reviewed head, or a push that changes only explainers.
Reviews now run at high instead of xhigh, and the review step stops after 30 minutes.
lines.say: Reviews now run at high instead of extra high, and the review step stops after thirty minutes.

lines.caption: A skipped review keeps the last reviewed commit, so the next review still covers what was skipped.
And the summary says when a review was stopped, or when CI's own fix still awaits its review.
Why: the review job billed 899 of about 2,000 minutes, much of it on fixes and replaced pushes.
lines.say: Why: the review job billed eight hundred ninety-nine of about two thousand minutes, much of it on fixes and replaced pushes.

lines.caption: Nothing goes unreviewed: the next review diffs from the last reviewed commit.
The author or subject alone isn't enough: the fix has to be recorded in the review state.
The agent never merges on CI's own fix. Its next push gets the fix reviewed, or with nothing to push, it asks you.
The PR changes the review script, the summary script, the workflow, and two instruction files.
To go back to deeper reviews, set the level back to xhigh in the workflow.
lines.say: To go back to deeper reviews, set the level back to extra high in the workflow.

lines.caption: Part 2. How it was built and verified.
The new rules sit beside the existing skip rules, and the review state needed no change.
Both new skips were tested with a scratch repository and a stand-in for GitHub. Each fired only when it should.
The whole plan step decided right in seven cases, and the push after a fix is reviewed from before the fix.
The summary says stopped only when the review job was cancelled.
How many minutes and findings the lighter review gives wasn't measured yet.
A local review found three small issues, and CI's first review found seven more. All were fixed.
The biggest change: a newer push is now spotted by its workflow run, which only a real push creates.
And CI's own fix must be recorded in the review state, and shows as not reviewed yet until the next push.
After the merge, the next fix commit and the next quick double push show the skips, and billing shows the savings.
Part 3. What comes later: build and job costs.
This is the second of four pull requests. Build costs come next, then fewer jobs.
Next, build and verify skip pull requests without code, and the compiler output is cached.
Last, the small jobs fold into bigger ones, and a push to main may reuse its pull request's build.
In short: the review skips work that's already covered, and every review is cheaper and capped.
